calibration.reference: Rozitis et al. (2013), A&A 555, A20, Table 3 ('Original' shape variant)
calibration.notes: Table 2 lists the fitted shape as 1022 vertices and 2040 facets with pole (48°, −72°) and period 3.065448 h from Ďurech et al. (2008a), the same counts, pole and period as DAMIT model 273. Table 3 gives 1.68 ± 0.09 km for this 'Original' shape. calibration.quantity: thermophysical volume-equivalent diameter fitted with this shape model
calibration.reference: DAMIT model 390 calibrated size, Hanuš et al. (2015), Icarus 256, 101
calibration.notes: DAMIT marks model 390 as size-calibrated by the thermophysical fit of Hanuš et al. (2015): D = 16.4 ± 1.3 km, thermal inertia 170 (90–260), geometric albedo 0.21 ± 0.04. The mirror pole, model 391, fits D = 16.8 ± 1.5 km. NEOWISE lists 15.812 ± 0.111 km (Masiero et al. 2014) and 17.739 ± 0.894 km (Masiero et al. 2012).
calibration.visibleDescription: Thermophysical diameter fitted to this mesh: 16.4 ± 1.3 km.

text.card: Largest piece of a family that broke up 5.8 million years ago.
text.introduction: M. Wolf found Karin at Heidelberg in 1916. It is the largest body of the Karin cluster, which formed in one break-up 5.8 million years ago.
text.shapeSummary: Shape from brightness changes as it spins, sized by a heat fit to this shape. The spin angle shown is arbitrary.

nesvorny-2002.label: Nesvorný et al. (2002), Nature 417, 720
nesvorny-2002.quote: As (832) Karin is the largest body in the observed population, we adopt the name ‘Karin cluster’.
nesvorny-2002.credit: D. Nesvorný, W. F. Bottke Jr, L. Dones, H. F. Levison

calibration.quantity: NEOWISE best-fit effective spherical diameter, transferred approximately to mesh volume diameter

text.card: Largest body of the Datura family.
text.introduction: G. Van Biesbroeck found Datura at Williams Bay in 1930. It is the largest body of the Datura family in the inner main belt.
text.shapeSummary: Shape from brightness changes as it spins, sized by an infrared survey. The spin angle shown is arbitrary.

datura-family.quote: A group of minor asteroids associated with the largest body Datura(1270) is of particular interest because it has enough known members and resides in the inner part of the main asteroid belt and is easy to observe.

text.card: Inner-belt asteroid that names the Hungaria group.
text.introduction: M. Wolf found Hungaria at Heidelberg in 1898. It may be where the aubrite meteorites come from.
text.shapeSummary: Shape from brightness changes as it spins, sized by an infrared survey. The spin angle shown is arbitrary.
